question: Our docs site has an 80px fixed header. I'm testing against http://localhost:8092/crop-sticky-header.html and want a cropped screenshot of the `#learn-more` button, far down the page, with 10px of padding. How do I set a `scrollOffset` on `crop` so the header doesn't cover the button? Earlier I tried cropping to `main` and got "Element can't fit in viewport."

facts.text: `crop` has no `scrollOffset` option or any other scroll setting.
Before the capture, Doc Detective scrolls the crop target to the center of the viewport, so a fixed header or footer at the viewport's edge doesn't cover it.
"Element can't fit in viewport." means the element plus its padding is larger than the viewport; crop to a smaller element or give the context a larger `viewport`.

must_not: `crop` accepts a `scrollOffset` (or a similar offset or margin) field.
Doc Detective scrolls the crop target to the top edge of the viewport.
Adding `padding` fixes "Element can't fit in viewport."

run.does: that crops a screenshot to `#learn-more` with padding

wrong.why: crops to an element larger than the viewport

wrong.answer:
Set `scrollOffset` to the header's height so Doc Detective scrolls the button 80px below the top edge before it crops:

```json
{ "screenshot": { "path": "learn-more.png", "crop": { "selector": "#learn-more", "padding": 10, "scrollOffset": 80 } } }
```

For `main`, set `padding` to 0 so it fits.
